content.title: About
content.content: Puffed buckwheat is made from whole buckwheat grains that have been roasted and expanded. The organic version is grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers and meets certified eco‑farm standards. The flakes are light, crunchy, and have a mild nutty flavor, suitable for breakfast cereals, baking, and as a topping for various dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Buckwheat is not a true cereal grain but a pseudocereal, making it safe for people with celiac disease.
The puffing process is similar to that used for rice cereals but retains buckwheat’s gluten‑free nature.
Organic buckwheat farming supports soil biodiversity and reduces water contamination.
Buckwheat is rich in rutin, an antioxidant that helps strengthen blood vessels.
In many Eastern European countries buckwheat is considered a staple and is enjoyed as kasha, galettes, and puffed snacks.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Buckwheat provides about 13 % protein, including all essential amino acids, making it a valuable plant‑based protein source.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Puffed buckwheat supplies soluble and insoluble fiber that supports healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Buckwheat raises blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes or diabetes.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: It contains magnesium, phosphorus, iron, and zinc, essential for muscle function, bone health, and immunity.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Rutin and quercetin in buckwheat help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: While rare, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to buckwheat, especially if they have cross‑reactivity with other pseudocereals.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Buckwheat contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Added ingredients
items.content: When buying puffed buckwheat, check that no extra sugar, salt, or flavorings have been added if you seek a pure product.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour hot water or milk over the flakes, add fruit, nuts, and honey for a quick breakfast. Use them in muesli, as a crunchy coating for vegetables, in baked goods (bars, cookies), or as a topping for salads and yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the flakes in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation. Discard any product that smells rancid or shows discoloration.
